description:

This 24-hour, on-site Capture The Flag (CTF) competition is designed to simulate real-world cybersecurity scenarios and evaluate participants' ability to solve complex security challenges under pressure.

Hosted at Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, the Grand Finale brings together the highest-performing teams for an intensive competition featuring advanced challenges across multiple cybersecurity domains. Participants will demonstrate their technical expertise, analytical thinking, teamwork, strategic decision-making, and adaptability while competing against some of the best cybersecurity talent.

Web Security
Cryptography
Reverse Engineering
Digital Forensics
Binary Exploitation (Pwn)
Open Source Intelligence (OSINT)
Steganography
Network Security
Miscellaneous Challenges

Throughout the competition, teams will work continuously for 24 hours, solving progressively challenging problems to accumulate points on the official scoreboard. The competition will conclude with score verification by the organizing committee, followed by the official announcement of winners during the Awards & Closing Ceremony.

The Grand Finale provides participants with an opportunity to showcase their cybersecurity skills in a highly competitive environment while networking with industry professionals, sponsors, security researchers, and fellow cybersecurity enthusiasts.

Mode: Offline
Venue: Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, Maharashtra, India
Duration: 24 Hours
Format: Advanced Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag (CTF)
Eligibility: Top 15 teams qualified from the Online Qualifier

title: HAM-DEFCON
location: National Institute Of Technology Warangal, Hanamkonda, Telangana, India, 505004
description:
HAM-DEFCON is a cybersecurity competition organized by HAM-ARC club of National Institute Of Technology Warangal Telangana, India.
Event Details:
Format: Attack & Defense
Categories: Web Exploitation, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and Infrastructure Hardening.
Team Size: 1–4 Members
Categories: Web Security, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), Reverse Engineering, Applied Cryptography, and Service Hardening

Rules & Code of Conduct
    On-Site & Network Access:
    The competition is strictly offline at the NIT Warangal campus. All team traffic and service interactions must route exclusively through the official network access gateway.

    Multi-Tiered Flagstores:
    Each service hosts multiple independent flagstores (Easy, Medium, Hard). Flags are dynamically rotated and refreshed every tick (round).

    Scoring Breakdown:

    Attack Points: Awarded for successfully exploiting opponent services and submitting their flags to the Flag Submission endpoint.

    Defense Points: Maintained by successfully patching vulnerabilities while keeping services operational.

    SLA (Uptime) Points: Awarded each round your services remain healthy, responsive, and passing all automated checker functionality tests.

    Scope & Infrastructure Immunity:
    Only designated opponent service ports and containers are in scope. Attacking the game engine, scoring backend, automated checkers, host hypervisors, or other teams’ network credentials will result in immediate disqualification.

    Fair Play & Service Integrity:
    Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks, network floods, deleting arbitrary system utilities, bricking service runtimes to prevent checker evaluation, and flag sharing or collusion between teams are strictly prohibited.
prizes: Winners got prizes upto 10K+ INR along with claude and codex subscriptions.

title: StealthCup 2026
location: On-site, Quebec City, Canada (Hackfest, Quebec City Convention Centre). Remote participation only on request.
description:
StealthCup is an evasion focused CTF and a research project by AIT, held this year at Hackfest in Quebec City. Most CTFs reward speed. StealthCup rewards staying invisible.

Teams attack a live IT and OT enterprise range while a real SOC stack watches. The team that reaches its objectives with the fewest severe detections wins. Up to 12 teams compete, each playing an IT part and an OT part, for the overall cup plus separate IT and OT cups. Detections are shown in real time so teams can adapt their evasion strategy. Resets of infrastructure and scores are possible but cost points.

Ideal team size is 4 to 8 players, with 2 to 4 on each side. The event is designed for professionals with a pentesting background, familiarity with evasion techniques, Windows and OT environments is an advantage. The event runs in English. Technical details and objectives are shared with confirmed teams a few days before the event.

Attack paths and evasion tricks from the event feed into detection research. The 2025 results were published at ACM AsiaCCS 2026. Winners join the StealthCup Hall of Fame and are published on the website, participants can opt for anonymity.

Registration: team registration at https://stealth.ait.ac.at/team-application/, individuals without a team at https://stealth.ait.ac.at/individual-registration/

Across more than 40 challenges and 8 disciplines, teams will investigate corrupted systems, recover hidden Reality Fragments, unlock classified dossiers, expose compromised actors, and gradually reconstruct the truth behind a phenomenon threatening the entire world.

Every flag matters.
Each solved challenge can reveal new intelligence, unlock characters and locations, alter the mission briefing, and move the story forward in real time. The competition platform becomes a living investigation that evolves with the progress of the Operators.

Expect  : 
- web exploitation, 
- digital forensics, 
- reverse engineering, 
- binary exploitation, 
- cryptography, 
- OSINT,

Built for teams from around the world and open to different experience levels, EyesOpenCTF is both a proving ground and an immersive narrative experience where competitors can learn, compete, get noticed, and join a fast-growing international cybersecurity community.

As part of EOCON, the competition also connects participants with experts, researchers, recruiters, entrepreneurs, and emerging talent from Africa and beyond. It is a place where technical ability meets storytelling, where discoveries change the mission, and where tomorrow’s collaborations, careers, and opportunities begin.

title: Cyber Ninja CTF 2026 - BLACKOUT
description:
RÉSERVÉ UNIQUEMENT AUX LYCÉENS

# Cyber Ninja CTF 2026 – BLACKOUT

Gardez Paris allumé !

Le Cyber Ninja CTF revient pour sa 3e édition avec BLACKOUT, une compétition nationale de cybersécurité organisée par OTERIA Cyber School et destinée aux lycéens de toute la France.

Cette année, un mystérieux hacker surnommé « Lights-Out » menace les infrastructures critiques de Paris : métro, électricité, réseaux de communication et distribution d'eau.

Votre mission : résoudre des challenges de cybersécurité, récupérer des flags, découvrir des indices cachés et arrêter Lights-Out avant que Paris ne soit plongé dans le noir.

## Dates et déroulement

Qualifications en ligne
- Début : samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 10h (heure de Paris)
- Fin : dimanche 22 novembre 2026 à 10h (heure de Paris)
- Durée : 24 heures
- Format : Jeopardy
- Participation : individuelle et gratuite

Finale en présentiel
- Date : samedi 16 janvier 2027
- Lieu : campus OTERIA, région parisienne
- Participants : les 80 meilleurs des qualifications éligibles
- Invité spécial : V2F, youtubeur spécialisé en cybersécurité

## Les challenges

Une cinquantaine de flags répartis dans 9 catégories :

- Web : exploitation de vulnérabilités Web
- PWN : exploitation de programmes binaires
- Reverse Engineering : rétro-ingénierie
- Crypto : cryptographie
- OSINT : recherche en sources ouvertes
- DFIR : investigation numérique et réponse aux incidents
- Hardware : sécurité matérielle
- Programming : programmation
- Misc : challenges divers

Trois niveaux de difficulté sont proposés : débutant, intermédiaire et confirmé.

Aucune expérience préalable en cybersécurité n'est nécessaire pour participer.

## Un scénario immersif : BLACKOUT

Pendant les qualifications, certains flags permettront de débloquer des éléments du dossier « Lights-Out » : messages interceptés, photographies, notes manuscrites et indices cachés.

Ces informations pourront aider les participants à progresser dans les challenges et à découvrir les prochaines cibles du hacker.

## Deux classements selon l'utilisation de l'IA

Au début de la compétition, chaque participant choisit son classement.

Classement sans IA agentique :
L'utilisation de l'IA comme assistant est autorisée, mais la résolution autonome des challenges par des agents IA est interdite. Seul ce classement permet de se qualifier pour la finale.

Classement avec IA :
Les outils d'intelligence artificielle, y compris les agents autonomes capables de résoudre entièrement des challenges, sont autorisés. Ce classement ne permet pas d'accéder à la finale.

## La grande finale

Les 80 meilleurs participants éligibles se retrouveront le 16 janvier 2027 sur le campus OTERIA pour une finale en présentiel.

Au programme :
- Des challenges inédits
- Un challenge exclusif conçu par V2F
- Une épreuve de sécurité matérielle
- La révélation du top 5 à 17h30
- La remise des récompenses

## Qui peut participer ?

Le Cyber Ninja CTF est exclusivement réservé aux lycéens.

- Inscription entièrement gratuite
- Participation à distance pour les qualifications
- Ouvert aux débutants comme aux passionnés
- Participation individuelle

## Organisation

Le Cyber Ninja CTF est organisé par OTERIA Cyber School, école spécialisée dans la cybersécurité.

Les challenges sont conçus par des étudiants et anciens étudiants d'OTERIA.

Site officiel :
https://www.cyber-ninja-ctf.fr/

Inscription :
https://www.cyber-ninja-ctf.fr/inscription

Prêt à relever le défi ? Rejoins Cyber Ninja CTF 2026 et empêche le BLACKOUT !
prizes:

title: CyberSci Regional Qualifiers 2026-27
description:

- Think you've got an elite team of students? Come and prove it. Our winners will go on to compete against the best in the world.
- Just starting out? This is the best way to learn and rise to the top.

Format:
- Modified jeopardy style. Realistic IT environment.
- Regional qualifiers are held in Nov-Dec each year.
- National finals are the following July.
- Winning teams represent Canada at international events in the Fall.

For Regionals (qualifiers):
We do hacking in the morning, interviews in the afternoon, and job offers by supper (for intern/summer/coop jobs).
- Full-time job offers take a few more days.
- Students register their team through their school instructor or computer club. Max 2 teams per school.

For nationals:
Participants will be the winning team from each regional/qualifier
- PLUS one all-juniors (19 and under)
- AND one all-women team (chosen from participants at the Regionals).
Two-day event.
prizes:
Winners at Regionals get instant interviews and sometimes same-day job offers.

Winners at Nationals will represent Canada at international events in the Fall.

title: CyberNSK2027-Qualifier
description:
CyberNSK 2027 is one of the largest cybersecurity competitions in Siberia, organized by Siberian Security League in collaboration with Novosibirsk State Technical University (NSTU NETI), Department of Information Security.

The online qualification round is a 12-hour Jeopardy-style CTF. Teams of up to 5 participants (school and university students) compete by solving practical security challenges and submitting flags.

✦ Start — November 28 at 12:00 PM (MSK)✦
✦ End — November 29 at 00:00 PM (MSK)✦

The competition uses a dynamic scoring system: the fewer teams solve a task, the more points it is worth.

Categories include:

Web

Crypto

Reverse Engineering

Pwn

Forensics

AI

Hardware

and others
prizes:
Top teams from the qualifiers will be invited to the on-site Attack-Defense finals in April 2027 in Novosibirsk:

April 17, 2027 — School finals

April 25, 2027 — University finals

CyberNSK focuses on real-world security skills, modern attack techniques, and practical defensive thinking.

title: BlackHat MEA CTF Final 2026
description:
Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) 2026 ?

The Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) is the largest cybersecurity competition in the region and officially the largest Capture The Flag competition in the world, recognized with a Guinness World Record. Organized by the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP) in collaboration with Black Hat MEA, the competition brings together thousands of cybersecurity professionals, researchers, students, and enthusiasts from around the globe.

Powered by the FlagYard platform, the competition follows a Jeopardy-style format, where teams of 3–5 players compete across a range of cybersecurity challenges, including Web Exploitation, PWN, Digital Forensics, Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and AI Hacking.

Competition Timeline

Registration: June 3 – August 29, 2026

Online Qualifiers: August 29, 2026 | 10:00 AM KSA (GMT+3) | Online

Thousands of participants will compete globally in teams of 3–5 members, with the top 150 teams qualifying for the final stage.

On-site Finals

The top 150 teams will be invited to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for a 3-day final competition during Black Hat MEA, taking place from December 1–3, 2026.

Register Now:
https://flagyard.com/events/3468f495-a92c-498b-90c2-994dfb99ea0b

Support: blackhatctf@safcsp.org.sa
prizes:
Prize Pool

Total Prize Pool: SAR 790,000 (Approx. USD 210,000)

Overall Winners

1st Place: SAR 300,000 (Approx. USD 80,000)
2nd Place: SAR 200,000 (Approx. USD 53,500)
3rd Place: SAR 100,000 (Approx. USD 26,500)
4th Place: SAR 60,000 (Approx. USD 16,000)
5th Place: SAR 40,000 (Approx. USD 10,500)

Local Team Awards

1st Local Team: SAR 40,000 (Approx. USD 10,500)
2nd Local Team: SAR 30,000 (Approx. USD 8,000)
3rd Local Team: SAR 20,000 (Approx. USD 5,300)
